render.intro: Sleep Prayer for a Grieving Heart

long1.title: Sleep Prayer for a Grieving Heart | When You're Missing Someone This Holiday (KJV)
long1.description:
A gentle guided sleep prayer for anyone grieving as the holidays begin, especially if there's an empty chair at your table this year. We remember that Jesus wept with His friends (John 11:35), that God keeps every tear (Psalm 56:8), that those who mourn are promised comfort (Matthew 5:4), and that He binds up the broken heart (Psalm 147:3). We give Him the words we never got to say, pray for the days ahead, and rest in the hope that weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning. After the prayer, about 18 minutes of quiet music stays with you while you fall asleep.

Scripture (KJV): John 11:35; Psalm 56:8; Matthew 5:4; Psalm 147:3; 1 Thessalonians 4:13; Revelation 21:4; Psalm 30:5; Psalm 4:8.

This prayer is not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.

long2.title: A Thanksgiving Night Prayer | Count Your Blessings and Rest in His Mercy (Psalm 136)
long2.description:
A slow, guided prayer of thanks for the end of Thanksgiving Day, however your day went. We remind our souls to "forget not all his benefits" (Psalm 103), thank God for the small gifts of food, warmth and rest (James 1:17), name the people we're grateful for (Philippians 1:3), give thanks for being carried through the hard places of this year (Psalm 116:12), pray Psalm 136 together with its refrain "his mercy endureth for ever", and remember those at quiet tables tonight. After the prayer, about 16 minutes of quiet music stays with you as you rest.

Scripture (KJV): Psalm 103:1-2; James 1:17; Philippians 1:3; Psalm 116:12; Psalm 136:1, 23; 2 Corinthians 9:15.

This prayer is not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.

long3.title: Advent Begins: Waiting with Hope | Isaiah 40 Explained (They That Wait Upon the LORD)
long3.description:
Advent begins this Sunday, the season of waiting for Christmas, and on the first Sunday we light the candle of hope. In this video we walk through Isaiah 40, a chapter written for God's people far from home in Babylon who wondered whether God had forgotten them. We look at "Comfort ye, comfort ye my people", the voice in the wilderness that the Gospels connect with John the Baptist, why "the word of our God shall stand for ever", the strong and gentle Shepherd, and the famous promise that "they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength". With an honest word for anyone in a waiting season, a prayer for the first week of Advent, and an invitation to our daily 24 Days to Christmas series starting December 1.

Scripture (KJV): Isaiah 40:1-11, 27-31; Lamentations 3:26.

This video is spiritual encouragement, not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.
